source_provenance.sourcePassage: Compile rate (i) barely responds to an intervention that substantially improves the generated code; (ii) is dominated by evaluation-harness and dataset artifacts rather than model quality, with about 64% of compile failures not attributable to the model, a share that is nearly invariant across models; (iii) shifts by 1.8 to 2.7 times on identical patches under a single compiler-standard flag, with zero regressions; (iv) ranks the three models in the opposite order to reference-similarity metrics; and (v) rewards non-repairs when used as an optimization target, since a compiler-feedback loop raises compile rate while similarity to the human fix falls, with manual inspection finding deletion- and placeholder-style non-repairs among the newly compiling outputs.

positions.text: Kaal's claim that more disclosure does not always mean better governance is qualified, not displaced, by a more targeted metric: a change-aware screen of the edited region can reduce some obvious proxy-gaming (zero credit to a no-op; near-zero credit to some, though not all, deletion-based gaming patches) while still crediting genuine partial edits, but the source treats that screen as a cheap preliminary filter before execution-based analysis, not as a repair-quality metric.
